acceptance_rule: Correctness, originality, and value must each pass.

correctness.rationale: The symbolic artifact reconstructs the cut-and-project Gram identities and the complete eight-vector shell. The interval certificate was inspected at the actual package path: it evaluates the octagonal-window Fourier integrals, uses the corrected \((-1)^j\) moment sign, encloses the cubic Taylor approximation on subintervals of a, and adds an explicit fourth-order remainder. All eight logged upper bounds are below -0.01160, leaving more than 0.004 margin to the claimed -0.0075 threshold. The resulting modulus and intensity lower bounds follow immediately. The general pure-point retention statement is also consistent with the deformation theorem for admissible Delone deformations.
correctness.risks: This is a source-audited interval certificate rather than a separate formal proof object; the claim is only for u=(1,0) and the named shell.

final_claim: For the stated equivariant sinusoidal deformation of the Ammann-Beenker model set with u=(1,0) and 0<=a<=1/4, every member of the eight-vector shell \(4|k|^2=17-12\sqrt{2}\) has Re A(k;a)<=-0.0075, hence intensity at least 3.515625e-6 and no extinction on that interval.

originality.broader_coverage: General deformation theorems preserve pure-point character and peak locations but allow intensities to change or vanish; they do not imply this peak remains nonzero.
originality.claim_vs_prior_implication: Pure-point retention is strictly weaker than a positive lower bound for a specified Bragg amplitude.
originality.equivalent_formulations: Checked deformed model sets, equivariant perturbations, Fourier-Bohr amplitudes, Bragg extinction/non-extinction, and Ammann-Beenker shell formulations.
originality.exact_database_or_table: No amplitude/extinction table for this deformation was located.
originality.rationale: Baake-Lenz prove preservation of pure-point diffraction under admissible equivariant deformations, and the deformed-model-set literature discusses transfer of Bragg intensities. Those results do not state non-extinction of this Ammann-Beenker shell under the package's sinusoidal deformation or the quantitative amplitude lower bound. Targeted searches found no source with the same deformation and shell certificate.
originality.risks: The phrase 'first observable' is conventional rather than an intrinsic least nonzero Fourier-module radius; the audited claim is tied to the explicitly named shell.

value.rationale: Extinction of a prominent eightfold Bragg shell under a natural equivariant deformation is a physically and mathematically motivated boundary question. A uniform certified lower intensity over a nontrivial deformation interval gives concrete information beyond the qualitative preservation of pure-point diffraction.
value.risks: The result is shell- and direction-specific and does not control all smaller Fourier-module vectors.
sources: Baake-Lenz deformation stability and deformed-model-set diffraction literature.
